planting.note: Plant container-grown or bare-root shrubs in early spring once the ground can be worked, in evenly moist to wet, well-drained soil.

directions: Elata is an older black chokeberry selection valued for producing noticeably larger flower clusters, leaves, and fruit than the wild species while keeping a tidy, rounded, more compacted habit instead of the looser spread typical of seed-grown plants. Grow it in full sun to light shade in consistently moist soil, where it tolerates both wet, heavy ground and short dry spells once established. The oversized white spring flower clusters give way to abundant purple-black berries that persist into winter for birds, while the glossy foliage still colors up red-orange in fall. Little pruning is needed beyond removing an occasional old cane to keep the rounded form open and productive.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant container-grown or bare-root shrubs in early spring in average to wet garden soil, giving it more room than compact landscape chokeberries since it grows into a larger shrub.

directions: Grandiflora is a vigorous, taller-growing black chokeberry selection distinguished by extra-large white spring flower clusters and heavy crops of edible black-purple berries, backed by purple-red fall foliage that is richer than the species' usual orange-red. It grows noticeably more upright and substantial than compact modern landscape cultivars, so it is best suited to the back of a border, a hedgerow, or a naturalized planting with room to fill in. Like other chokeberries it adapts equally well to wet, poorly drained soil and average garden conditions, tolerating light shade though fruiting and fall color are strongest in full sun. Renewal-prune a portion of the oldest stems every few years on established plants to keep them well-furnished with vigorous fruiting wood.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Plant Toolbox
